# The Lasso

## Intention

```{r}

library(rio)

# Clean the names
coef_names <- c(  
  "NumberChildren" = "Number of children in the household",
  "Taux.de.couv.global" = "Early childcare coverage in the area of residence",
  "ActiveYes" = "Mother is active before birth",
  "WorkPlanToYes" = "Mother wanted to work after birth",
  "ECAccessHoursFitYes" = "Early childcare opening hours fit",
  "AccessInformalFullTimeYes" = "Houshold has access to informal full-time childcare",
  "OpportunityCosts" = "Opportunity costs of staying at home for the mother",
  "NegativeImpactSalaryYes" = "Perceived negative impact of staying at home on salary",
  "NegativeImpactCareerYes" = "Perceived negative impact of staying at home on career",
  "NegativeImpactWellBeingYes" = "Perceived negative impact of staying at home on well-being",
  "PrescriptiveNorm" = "Number of people opposed to mother using childcare",
  "NormsUseMostToAllYes" = "The majority of friends and relatives use early childcare",
  "AttitudesTowardsWorkAndFamilyYes" = "Traditional attitudes towards household roles",
  "AttitudesLaborAffectsChildrenYes" = "Believes work negatively affects children",
  "PerceivedAffordabilityOverestimate" = "Overestimates affordability of early childcare",
  "PerceivedAffordabilityUnderestimate" = "Underestimates affordability of early childcare",
  "TrustEarlyChildcareAgreeYes" = "Household trusts early childcare",
  "ECBenefitChildrenAgreeYes" = "Household believes in early childcare benefits",
  "LevelInformationLow knowledge" = "Household has low knowledge about early childcare",
  "LevelComprehensionGoodExcellentYes" = "Mother's comprehension level of French is good/excellent",
  "PresentOrientedYes" = "The mother is present biased",
  "KnowsECIsSubsidizedYes" = "Household knows that early childcare is subsidized",
  "BelieveAccessingChildcareEasyYes" = "Household believes accessing childcare is easy",
  "HasAccessToAComputerYes" = "Household has access to a computer",
  "CanAccessScoialResourcesYes" = "Household can access social resources",
  "CanAccessInformationYes" = "Household can access information", 
   "ActivityCriteriaYesYes" = "Active mothers are prioritized",
  "SocialCriteriaYesYes" = "Vulnerable families are prioritized",
  "RegistrationOnlineOnlyYes" = "Registration is online only" 
 # "EntryAgeBeforeOneBeforeOne" = "Household want to use early childcare after the child is 1 yo" # Dropped becuse colinear
)


lasso_clean <- MLDummified %>% filter(!is.na(Intention)) %>% 
  mutate(target = as.numeric(Intention) - 1) %>%
 select(-c(Assignment, ECSApp, ECSUseYes, Intention, EntryAgeBeforeOne,BabyHealthIndex, MotherHealthIndex, MovedOut))%>%      
  mutate(across(where(is.logical), as.numeric)) 

# Cleaning the data

# Create a subset with the sociodemo and the predictors
# Cleaning the data



# Preparation
## Split the sample
library(tidymodels)
tidymodels_prefer()
set.seed(30)
lasso_split <- initial_split(lasso_clean, prop = 0.8)
lasso_train <- training(lasso_split)
lasso_test <- testing(lasso_split)

# Apply the recipe (simplified)
model_recipe <- recipe(target ~ ., data = lasso_train) %>%
  step_unknown(AttitudesTowardsWorkAndFamily, 
               AttitudesLaborAffectsChildren) %>% 
    step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE) %>%
    step_zv() %>%
    step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) %>% 
   step_impute_knn(
                  Taux.de.couv.global,
                  NumberChildren,
                  PrescriptiveNorm,
                  neighbors = 5) %>% 
  step_YeoJohnson(
                  NumberChildren, 
                  OpportunityCosts,

                  PrescriptiveNorm
                  #BreastFeedLength,
                  #NumberChildren
                  )  # some variables are skewed. We transform them using YeoJohson that can also deal with missing values


# Model specification
lasso_spec <-  linear_reg(penalty = tune(), # here we need something new
                          mixture = 1) %>% # penalty is the lambda parameter
  # mixture is the alpha. Alpha = 1 is just the lasso
  # Penalty is tune ()
  set_mode("regression") %>% # we are still doing regression
  set_engine("glmnet") # we use a different engine that does regularisation

lasso_wf <- workflow() %>% # define the workflow
  add_model(lasso_spec) %>%
  add_recipe(model_recipe)

elastic_metrics <- metric_set(rsq) # we select metrics, we don't want the 3
# we use the rsq metric

# Resampling methods: 10 fold cross-validation
set.seed(20)
cv_folds <- vfold_cv(lasso_train,
                     v = 10,
                     repeats = 5)

# Using dials to tune the model: 
glmnet_param <- extract_parameter_set_dials(lasso_spec)# it extracts for me the parameter that 
# needs to be tuned

# Set the grid
set.seed(15)
lasso_grid <- grid_max_entropy(glmnet_param,
                               size = 175, # generate 50 different lambdas
                               # 50 is a bit low, 100 or 150 is better
                               original = TRUE, # we are keeoing the original scale, the log
                               variogram_range = 0.5) # the higher the value, the less likely it is to explore 


# Tuning the Hyper-Parameter
doParallel::registerDoParallel() # to know how many cores to use at the same time
lasso_tune <- lasso_wf %>%
  tune_grid(cv_folds,
            grid = lasso_grid, # use the grid we just created
            metrics = elastic_metrics)
# So far we've selected 50 values of lambda. It run a regression for each lambda within each fold
# We are running 50 * 10 * 5 = 2500 regressions in total, which all has a different R2

# Plot the (average) performance
autoplot(lasso_tune) # x is different values of lambda in the log scale. y is the average R2

# Select the best lambda
lasso_best <- select_best(lasso_tune)
lasso_best # Model 46 

temp <- collect_metrics(lasso_tune)
# the std error is the variance divided by the square root of N
# We see that model 46 is the best, but we can also see that the difference between the best and the worst is not that big

# Finalizing the fit
lasso_updated <- finalize_model(lasso_spec, # I finalize by using the pre specified moded
                                lasso_best) # this replace the spec() argument by the picked lambda
workflow_new <- lasso_wf %>%
  update_model(lasso_updated)

new_fit <- workflow_new %>%
  fit(data = lasso_train)

tidy_lasso <- new_fit %>%
  extract_fit_parsnip() %>%
  tidy()


# Evaluating the model: performance
lasso_metrics <- new_fit %>%
  predict(lasso_test) %>%
  bind_cols(lasso_test) %>%
  metrics(truth = target, estimate = .pred)


## POST LASSO 

lasso_var <- tidy_lasso %>% 
  filter(estimate != 0) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  pull(term)  # Liste des variables sélectionnées


## Post Lasso on training and test sets

# Appliquer la recipe sur les données d'entraînement
lasso_train_baked <- prep(model_recipe) %>% # we preprosess the data
  bake(new_data = lasso_train) # it creates the transformed dataset  

# We do the same for the test set 
lasso_test_baked <- prep(model_recipe) %>% # should we apply the transformatios ? 
  bake(new_data = lasso_test)

# Select only the variables that the lasso picked up
lasso_train_post <- lasso_train_baked %>%
  select(all_of(c("target", lasso_var))) # we select the target and the variables that the lasso picked up

lasso_test_post <- lasso_test_baked %>% # for model metrics
  select(all_of(c("target", lasso_var)))

# Fit the model on the training set 
post_lasso_model <- lm(target ~ ., data = lasso_train_post)


# Accuracy on the test set based on the predicted coefficient
post_lasso_preds <- predict(post_lasso_model, newdata = lasso_test_post)

# Calculer les métriques
post_lasso_metrics <- metrics(
  data = data.frame(truth = lasso_test_post$target, estimate = post_lasso_preds),
  truth = truth,
  estimate = estimate
)

print(post_lasso_metrics)

### Test with the whole dataset
# Appliquer la recipe sur les données d'entraînement
lasso_train_baked <- prep(model_recipe) %>% # we preprosess the data
  bake(new_data = lasso_clean) # it creates the dataset normalized and transformed


# Select only the variables that the lasso picked up
lasso_train_post <- lasso_train_baked %>%
  select(all_of(c("target", lasso_var))) # we select the target and the variables that the lasso picked up

# Fit the model on the training set 
post_lasso_model <- lm(target ~ ., data = lasso_train_post)

library(broom)      # Pour tidy()
library(dplyr)      # Pour manipuler les données
library(knitr)      # Pour knitr::kable
library(kableExtra) # Pour styliser les tableaux

# Extraire les coefficients et autres informations du modèle
coefficients_table <- tidy(post_lasso_model) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(estimate))) %>% # Trier par ordre décroissant de la valeur absolue des coefficients
  mutate(estimate = round(estimate, 3),  # Arrondir pour améliorer la lisibilité
         std.error = round(std.error, 3))
# Sélectionner les colonnes importantes

## Générer un joli tableau pour Word
#coefficients_table %>%
#  kable(format = "html", col.names = c("Variable", "Coefficient", "Erreur standard", "P-value"), 
#        caption = "Tableau des coefficients du modèle Lasso") %>%
#  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
#
library(modelsummary)

## PLOTS
# 1. Extraire et trier les coefficients avec broom::tidy
tidied <- tidy(post_lasso_model) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(estimate))) # Trier par ordre décroissant de la valeur absolue des coefficients
  
# TO DO LATER: Clean the names
  # Sort coefficients by absolute value
  #sorted_coefficients <- tidy(post_lasso_model) %>%
   # arrange(desc(abs(estimate))) %>%
    #filter(term != "(Intercept)")
  
  # Create vector with sorted names
 # sorted_names <- sorted_coefficients$term
  
  # Order coefficient map including intercept

#  ordered_coef_map <- coef_names[c("(Intercept)", sorted_names)]

# 2. Utiliser coef_map pour réorganiser les coefficients dans modelsummary
modelsummary(list("Intention" =post_lasso_model),
             statistic = "{std.error} ({p.value})",
             estimate="{estimate}{stars}  [{conf.low}, {conf.high}]",
             coef_map = setNames(tidied$term, tidied$term), # Réorganiser les coefficients dans l'ordre trié    

             #gof_map = c("nobs", "r.squared", "adj.r.squared", "AIC", "BIC"), # Inclure les statistiques globales
             stars = c("***"=.01,"**"=.05,"*"=.1),
              output = 'flextable') %>% autofit()


# Forest plot
out_conf <- tidy(post_lasso_model, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  filter(!is.na(conf.low)) %>%  # Filtrer les NA des intervalles de confiance
  filter(term != "(Intercept)")  # Enlever l'intercept

lm_model_out <- round_df(out_conf, digits=2)

# Now plot them
ggplot(lm_model_out, aes(x=reorder(term, estimate), y=estimate)) +
         geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=conf.low, ymax=conf.high), 
                       width = 0.2, size = 1,
                       position = "dodge", color="turquoise4") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red", size = 1) +
  geom_point() + 
  coord_flip()+
     theme_minimal() +
     theme(
       axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
       plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
       axis.title = element_text(size = 12)
     ) +
     labs(
       title = "Determinants of Early Childcare Intention",
       subtitle = "Post-LASSO predictors",
       x = "",
       y = "Coefficient Estimates"
     )

```

### Oaxaca Blinder

```{r}

# extract the name of the coefficient 
lasso_var_intention <- clean_variable_names(lasso_var)


# Prepare the data for Oaxaca-Blinder
oaxaca_data_intention <- Oaxaca %>%
  filter(!is.na(Intention)) %>%
  mutate(
    target = as.numeric(Intention) - 1,
    Educ_bin = as.numeric(Educ == "Sup")) %>%   # Convert to binary: 1 for "Sup", 0 for "Bac"=) %>%
  select(target, Educ_bin, all_of(lasso_var_intention)) 


# Create formula using clean_vars with proper oaxaca syntax
formula_vars <- paste(lasso_var_intention, collapse = " + ")
formula_str <- paste("target ~ ", formula_vars, " | Educ_bin")
oax_formula <- as.formula(formula_str)

set.seed(124)
 # Level of comprehension creates pb
# Run Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition
oax_lasso_intention <- oaxaca(formula = oax_formula,
                     data = oaxaca_data_intention,
                     R = 100)  # Number of bootstrap repetitions

# Plot the share of the gap explained by the variables
gapExplained <- plot_oaxaca_gap(oax_lasso_intention, 
                                outcome = "Intention",
                                model = "Post-Lasso predictors")
gapExplained



```

## Application

```{r}

library(rio)



lasso_clean <- MLDummified %>%
  filter(!is.na(ECSApp)) %>%
  mutate(target = as.numeric(ECSApp))  %>%  # the idea db we would be working with in the end
 select(-c( ECSApp, ECSUseYes))%>%      
  mutate(across(where(is.logical), as.numeric)) 



# Preparation
## Split the sample
library(tidymodels)
tidymodels_prefer()
set.seed(10)
lasso_split <- initial_split(lasso_clean, prop = 0.8)
lasso_train <- training(lasso_split)
lasso_test <- testing(lasso_split)

# Apply the recipe (simplified)
model_recipe <- recipe(target ~ ., data = lasso_train) %>%
  step_unknown(EntryAgeBeforeOne,
               AttitudesTowardsWorkAndFamily, AttitudesLaborAffectsChildren
               #FmlyIncomeBaseline,
                # IncomeBaseline, 
           #    TrustCreche, 
            #   DeprivHolidays,
               #BreastFeedIntend,
            #   InformalReciprocity, 
             #TrustAssMat,
             #TrustFam,
            # TrustFriend,
             #CoupleCohabiting,
             #AccessEasy5, 
             #NormsHouse, 
#NormsWork, 
#LevelInfoSubExPost, 
#Assignment
) %>%   step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE) %>%
    step_zv() %>%
    step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) %>% 
   step_impute_knn(all_numeric_predictors(), neighbors = 5) %>%
  step_YeoJohnson(
                  MotherHealthIndex,
                  BabyHealthIndex,
                  NumberChildren, 
                  OpportunityCosts,

                  PrescriptiveNorm
                  ) # some variables are skewed. We transform them using YeoJohson that can also deal with missing values

# Model specification
lasso_spec <-  linear_reg(penalty = tune(), # here we need something new
                          mixture = 1) %>% # penalty is the lambda parameter
  # mixture is the alpha. Alpha = 1 is just the lasso
  # Penalty is tune ()
  set_mode("regression") %>% # we are still doing regression
  set_engine("glmnet") # we use a different engine that does regularisation

lasso_wf <- workflow() %>% # define the workflow
  add_model(lasso_spec) %>%
  add_recipe(model_recipe)

elastic_metrics <- metric_set(rsq) # we select metrics, we don't want the 3
# we use the rsq metric

# Resampling methods: 10 fold cross-validation
set.seed(20)
cv_folds <- vfold_cv(lasso_train,
                     v = 10,
                     repeats = 5)

# Using dials to tune the model: 
glmnet_param <- extract_parameter_set_dials(lasso_spec)# it extracts for me the parameter that 
# needs to be tuned

# Set the grid
set.seed(15)
lasso_grid <- grid_max_entropy(glmnet_param,
                               size = 175, # generate 50 different lambdas
                               # 50 is a bit low, 100 or 150 is better
                               original = TRUE, # we are keeoing the original scale, the log
                               variogram_range = 0.5) # the higher the value, the less likely it is to explore 



# Tuning the Hyper-Parameter
doParallel::registerDoParallel() # to know how many cores to use at the same time
lasso_tune <- lasso_wf %>%
  tune_grid(cv_folds,
            grid = lasso_grid, # use the grid we just created
            metrics = elastic_metrics)
# So far we've selected 50 values of lambda. It run a regression for each lambda within each fold
# We are running 50 * 10 * 5 = 2500 regressions in total, which all has a different R2

# Plot the (average) performance
autoplot(lasso_tune) # x is different values of lambda in the log scale. y is the average R2

# Select the best lambda
lasso_best <- select_best(lasso_tune)
lasso_best # Model 46 

temp <- collect_metrics(lasso_tune)
# the std error is the variance divided by the square root of N
# We see that model 46 is the best, but we can also see that the difference between the best and the worst is not that big

# Finalizing the fit
lasso_updated <- finalize_model(lasso_spec, # I finalize by using the pre specified moded
                                lasso_best) # this replace the spec() argument by the picked lambda
workflow_new <- lasso_wf %>%
  update_model(lasso_updated)

new_fit <- workflow_new %>%
  fit(data = lasso_train)

tidy_lasso <- new_fit %>%
  extract_fit_parsnip() %>%
  tidy()


# Evaluating the model: performance
metrics <- new_fit %>%
  predict(lasso_test) %>%
  bind_cols(lasso_test) %>%
  metrics(truth = target, estimate = .pred)


## POST LASSO 

lasso_var_application <- tidy_lasso %>% 
  filter(estimate != 0) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  pull(term)  # Liste des variables sélectionnées




## Post Lasso on training and test sets

# Appliquer la recipe sur les données d'entraînement
lasso_train_baked <- prep(model_recipe) %>% # we preprosess the data
  bake(new_data = lasso_train) # it creates the transformed dataset  

# We do the same for the test set 
lasso_test_baked <- prep(model_recipe) %>% # should we apply the transformatios ? 
  bake(new_data = lasso_test)

# Select only the variables that the lasso picked up
lasso_train_post <- lasso_train_baked %>%
  select(all_of(c("target", lasso_var_application))) # we select the target and the variables that the lasso picked up

lasso_test_post <- lasso_test_baked %>% # for model metrics
  select(all_of(c("target", lasso_var_application)))

# Fit the model on the training set

# Accuracy on the test set based on the predicted coefficient
post_lasso_preds <- predict(post_lasso_model, newdata = lasso_test_post)

# Calculer les métriques
post_lasso_metrics <- metrics(
  data = data.frame(truth = lasso_test_post$target, estimate = post_lasso_preds),
  truth = truth,
  estimate = estimate
)
print(post_lasso_metrics)

### Test with the whole dataset

lasso_train_baked <- prep(model_recipe) %>% # we preprosess the data
  bake(new_data = lasso_clean) # it creates the dataset normalized and transformed


# Select only the variables that the lasso picked up
lasso_train_post <- lasso_train_baked %>%
  select(all_of(c("target", lasso_var_application))) # we select the target and the variables that the lasso picked up

# Fit the model on the training set 
post_lasso_model <- lm(target ~ ., data = lasso_train_post)



# Extraire les coefficients et autres informations du modèle
coefficients_table <- tidy(post_lasso_model) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(estimate))) %>% # Trier par ordre décroissant de la valeur absolue des coefficients
  mutate(estimate = round(estimate, 3),  # Arrondir pour améliorer la lisibilité
         std.error = round(std.error, 3))
# Sélectionner les colonnes importantes

## Générer un joli tableau pour Word

#  kable(format = "html", col.names = c("Variable", "Coefficient", "Erreur standard", "P-value"), 
#        caption = "Tableau des coefficients du modèle Lasso") %>%
#  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
#


# 1. Extraire et trier les coefficients avec broom::tidy
tidied <- tidy(post_lasso_model) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(estimate))) # Trier par ordre décroissant de la valeur absolue des coefficients

# 2. Utiliser coef_map pour réorganiser les coefficients dans modelsummary
modelsummary(list("Application" =post_lasso_model),
             statistic = "{std.error} ({p.value})",
             estimate="{estimate}{stars}  [{conf.low}, {conf.high}]",
             coef_map = setNames(tidied$term, tidied$term), # Réorganiser les coefficients dans l'ordre trié
             #gof_map = c("nobs", "r.squared", "adj.r.squared", "AIC", "BIC"), # Inclure les statistiques globales
             stars = c("***"=.01,"**"=.05,"*"=.1),
              output = 'flextable') %>% autofit()



# Forest plot
out_conf <- tidy(post_lasso_model, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  filter(!is.na(conf.low)) %>%  # Filtrer les NA des intervalles de confiance
  filter(term != "(Intercept)")  # Enlever l'intercept

lm_model_out <- round_df(out_conf, digits=2)

# Now plot them
ggplot(lm_model_out, aes(x=reorder(term, estimate), y=estimate)) +
         geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=conf.low, ymax=conf.high), 
                       width = 0.2, size = 1,
                       position = "dodge", color="turquoise4") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red", size = 1) +
  geom_point() + 
  coord_flip()+
     theme_minimal() +
     theme(
       axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
       plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
       axis.title = element_text(size = 12)
     ) +
     labs(
       title = "Determinants of Early Childcare Application",
       subtitle = "Post-LASSO predictors",
       x = "",
       y = "Coefficient Estimates"
     )

```

## Access 

```{r}

lasso_clean <- MLDummified_Access %>%   
  filter(!is.na(ECSUseYes)) %>%
  mutate(target = as.numeric(ECSUseYes), 
         Applied = ifelse(ECSApp == 1, "Yes", "No"), 
         Applied = factor(Applied, labels = c("No", "Yes"))
                          ) %>% 
  select( -c(ECSUseYes, ECSApp, EntryAgeBeforeOne))  # Take a look at the data with skimr 



# Preparation 
## Split the sample 
set.seed(10) 
lasso_split <- initial_split(lasso_clean, prop = 0.8) 
lasso_train <- training(lasso_split) 
lasso_test <- testing(lasso_split)  # Apply the recipe (simplified) 

  

model_recipe <- recipe(target ~ ., data = lasso_train) %>%  
  step_unknown(#EntryAgeBeforeOne, 
                 AttitudesTowardsWorkAndFamily, AttitudesLaborAffectsChildren) %>%   
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE) %>%
    step_zv() %>%
    step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) %>% 
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) %>% 
 step_impute_knn(Taux.de.couv.global,
                NumberChildren,
                PrescriptiveNorm,
                neighbors = 5) %>% 
  step_YeoJohnson(MotherHealthIndex,
                  BabyHealthIndex,
                  NumberChildren, 
                  MonthlyDaycareFees,
                  PrescriptiveNorm
                  )



# Clean the names
coef_names_access <- c(
  "IntentionYes" = "Intention: Household wants to use early childcare after birth",
  "NumberChildren" = "Number of children in the household",
  "Taux.de.couv.global" = "Early childcare coverage in the area of residence",
  "ActiveYes" = "Mother is active before birth",
  "WorkPlanToYes" = "Mother wanted to work after birth",
  "ECAccessHoursFitYes" = "Early childcare opening hours fit",
  "AccessInformalFullTimeYes" = "Houshold has access to informal full-time childcare",
  #"OpportunityCosts" = "Opportunity costs of staying at home for the mother",
  "MonthlyDaycareFees" = "Monthly daycare fees",
  "NegativeImpactSalaryYes" = "Perceived negative impact of staying at home on salary",
  "NegativeImpactCareerYes" = "Perceived negative impact of staying at home on career",
  "NegativeImpactWellBeingYes" = "Perceived negative impact of staying at home on well-being",
  "PrescriptiveNorm" = "Number of people opposed to mother using childcare",
  "NormsUseMostToAllYes" = "The majority of friends and relatives use early childcare",
  "AttitudesTowardsWorkAndFamilyYes" = "Traditional attitudes towards household roles",
  "AttitudesLaborAffectsChildrenYes" = "Believes work negatively affects children",
  "PerceivedAffordabilityOverestimate" = "Overestimates affordability of early childcare",
  "PerceivedAffordabilityUnderestimate" = "Underestimates affordability of early childcare",
  "TrustEarlyChildcareAgreeYes" = "Household trusts early childcare",
  "ECBenefitChildrenAgreeYes" = "Household believes in early childcare benefits",
  "LevelInformationLow knowledge" = "Household has low knowledge about early childcare",
  "LevelComprehensionGoodExcellentYes" = "Mother's comprehension level of French is good/excellent",
  "PresentOrientedYes" = "The mother is present biased",
  "KnowsECIsSubsidizedYes" = "Household knows that early childcare is subsidized",
  "BelieveAccessingChildcareEasyYes" = "Household believes accessing childcare is easy",
  "HasAccessToAComputerYes" = "Household has access to a computer",
  "CanAccessScoialResourcesYes" = "Household can access social resources",
  "CanAccessInformationYes" = "Household can access information",
  "MotherHealthIndex" = "Mother's health index at endline",
  "BabyHealthIndex" = "Baby's health index at endline",
  "AssignmentT1" = "Received Information only",
  "AssignmentT2" = "Received Information + Support",
  #"EntryAgeBeforeOneBefore One" = "Want to use early childcare before the child is 1 yo", 
  "AppliedYes" = "Applied to early childcare at endline",
  #"PoliticalOrientationRight" = "Right-wing mayor",
  #"PoliticalOrientationOther" = "Other political orientation of the mayor",
 "MovedOutYes" = "Household moved between baseline and endline", 
 "ECSAppTimingBeforeBirthYes" = "Applied before birth",
 "IncomeLess than 1500 euros" = "Household income earns less than 1500 euros",
 "IncomeMore than 2500 euros" = "Household income more than 2500 euros", 
       "ApplicationCalledYes" = "Household contacted providers by phone", 
      "ApplicationWentOnSiteYesYes" = "Household visited providers in person",
      "ApplicationNetworkedYes" = "Household reached out to an elected official", 
   "ActivityCriteriaYesYes" = "Active mothers are prioritized",
  "SocialCriteriaYesYes" = "Vulnerable families are prioritized",
  "RegistrationOnlineOnlyYes" = "Registration is online only"
)


# Model specification
lasso_spec <-  linear_reg(penalty = tune(), # here we need something new
                          mixture = 1) %>% # penalty is the lambda parameter
  # mixture is the alpha. Alpha = 1 is just the lasso
  # Penalty is tune ()
  set_mode("regression") %>% # we are still doing regression
  set_engine("glmnet") # we use a different engine that does regularisation

lasso_wf <- workflow() %>% # define the workflow
  add_model(lasso_spec) %>%
  add_recipe(model_recipe)

elastic_metrics <- metric_set(rsq) # we select metrics, we don't want the 3
# we use the rsq metric

# Resampling methods: 10 fold cross-validation
set.seed(20)
cv_folds <- vfold_cv(lasso_train,
                     v = 10,
                     repeats = 5)

# Using dials to tune the model: 
glmnet_param <- extract_parameter_set_dials(lasso_spec)# it extracts for me the parameter that 
# needs to be tuned

# Set the grid
set.seed(15)
lasso_grid <- grid_max_entropy(glmnet_param,
                               size = 175, # generate 50 different lambdas
                               # 50 is a bit low, 100 or 150 is better
                               original = TRUE, # we are keeoing the original scale, the log
                               variogram_range = 0.5) # the higher the value, the less likely it is to explore 

# Vérifier que la recette fonctionne
#prep(model_recipe) %>%
#  bake(new_data = NULL) %>%
#  glimpse()

# Tuning the Hyper-Parameter
doParallel::registerDoParallel() # to know how many cores to use at the same time
lasso_tune <- lasso_wf %>%
  tune_grid(cv_folds,
            grid = lasso_grid, # use the grid we just created
            metrics = elastic_metrics)
# So far we've selected 50 values of lambda. It run a regression for each lambda within each fold
# We are running 50 * 10 * 5 = 2500 regressions in total, which all has a different R2

# Plot the (average) performance
autoplot(lasso_tune) # x is different values of lambda in the log scale. y is the average R2

# Select the best lambda
lasso_best <- select_best(lasso_tune)
lasso_best # Model 46 

temp <- collect_metrics(lasso_tune)
# the std error is the variance divided by the square root of N
# We see that model 46 is the best, but we can also see that the difference between the best and the worst is not that big

# Finalizing the fit
lasso_updated <- finalize_model(lasso_spec, # I finalize by using the pre specified moded
                                lasso_best) # this replace the spec() argument by the picked lambda
workflow_new <- lasso_wf %>%
  update_model(lasso_updated)

new_fit <- workflow_new %>%
  fit(data = lasso_train)

tidy_lasso <- new_fit %>%
  extract_fit_parsnip() %>%
  tidy()


lasso_var = tidy_lasso %>% filter(estimate != 0)
# Evaluating the model: performance
metrics <- new_fit %>%
  predict(lasso_test) %>%
  bind_cols(lasso_test) %>%
  metrics(truth = target, estimate = .pred)


lasso_var_access <- tidy_lasso %>% 
  filter(estimate != 0) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  pull(term)  # Liste des variables sélectionnées



## Post Lasso on training and test sets

# Appliquer la recipe sur les données d'entraînement
lasso_train_baked <- prep(model_recipe) %>% # we preprosess the data
  bake(new_data = lasso_train) # it creates the transformed dataset  

# We do the same for the test set 
lasso_test_baked <- prep(model_recipe) %>% # should we apply the transformatios ? 
  bake(new_data = lasso_test)

# Select only the variables that the lasso picked up
lasso_train_post <- lasso_train_baked %>%
  select(all_of(c("target", lasso_var_access))) # we select the target and the variables that the lasso picked up

lasso_test_post <- lasso_test_baked %>% # for model metrics
  select(all_of(c("target", lasso_var_access)))

# Fit the model on the training set 
post_lasso_model <- lm(target ~ ., data = lasso_train_post)


# Accuracy on the test set based on the predicted coefficient
post_lasso_preds <- predict(post_lasso_model, newdata = lasso_test_post)

# Calculer les métriques
post_lasso_metrics <- metrics(
  data = data.frame(truth = lasso_test_post$target, estimate = post_lasso_preds),
  truth = truth,
  estimate = estimate
)
print(post_lasso_metrics)

### Test with the whole dataset
# Appliquer la recipe sur les données d'entraînement
lasso_train_baked <- prep(model_recipe) %>% # we preprosess the data
  bake(new_data = lasso_clean) # it creates the dataset normalized and transformed


# Select only the variables that the lasso picked up
lasso_train_post <- lasso_train_baked %>%
  select(all_of(c("target", lasso_var_access))) # we select the target and the variables that the lasso picked up

# Fit the model on the training set 
post_lasso_model <- lm(target ~ ., data = lasso_train_post)


# Extraire les coefficients et autres informations du modèle
coefficients_table <- tidy(post_lasso_model) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(estimate))) %>% # Trier par ordre décroissant de la valeur absolue des coefficients
  mutate(estimate = round(estimate, 3),  # Arrondir pour améliorer la lisibilité
         std.error = round(std.error, 3))
# Sélectionner les colonnes importantes

## Générer un joli tableau pour Word
#coefficients_table %>%
#  kable(format = "html", col.names = c("Variable", "Coefficient", "Erreur standard", "P-value"), 
#        caption = "Tableau des coefficients du modèle Lasso") %>%
#  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
#


# 1. Extraire et trier les coefficients avec broom::tidy
tidied <- tidy(post_lasso_model) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(estimate))) # Trier par ordre décroissant de la valeur absolue des coefficients

# 2. Utiliser coef_map pour réorganiser les coefficients dans modelsummary
modelsummary(list("Access" = post_lasso_model),
             statistic = "{std.error} ({p.value})",
             estimate="{estimate}{stars}  [{conf.low}, {conf.high}]",
             coef_map = setNames(tidied$term, tidied$term), # Réorganiser les coefficients dans l'ordre trié
             #gof_map = c("nobs", "r.squared", "adj.r.squared", "AIC", "BIC"), # Inclure les statistiques globales
             stars = c("***"=.01,"**"=.05,"*"=.1),
              output = 'flextable')


# Forest plot
out_conf <- tidy(post_lasso_model, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  filter(!is.na(conf.low)) %>%  # Filtrer les NA des intervalles de confiance
  filter(term != "(Intercept)")  # Enlever l'intercept

lm_model_out <- round_df(out_conf, digits=2)

# Now plot them
ggplot(lm_model_out, aes(x=reorder(term, estimate), y=estimate)) +
         geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=conf.low, ymax=conf.high), 
                       width = 0.2, size = 1,
                       position = "dodge", color="turquoise4") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red", size = 1) +
  geom_point() + 
  coord_flip()+
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 12)
    ) +
    labs(
      title = "Determinants of Early Childcare Access",
      subtitle = "Post-LASSO predictors",
      x = "",
      y = "Coefficient Estimates"
    )
```

```{r}
  arrange(desc(abs(estimate))) # Trier par ordre décroissant de la valeur absolue des coefficients

# 2. Utiliser coef_map pour réorganiser les coefficients dans modelsummary
modelsummary(list("Access" = post_lasso_model),
             statistic = "{std.error} ({p.value})",
             estimate="{estimate}{stars}  [{conf.low}, {conf.high}]",
             coef_map = setNames(tidied$term, tidied$term), # Réorganiser les coefficients dans l'ordre trié
             #gof_map = c("nobs", "r.squared", "adj.r.squared", "AIC", "BIC"), # Inclure les statistiques globales
             stars = c("***"=.01,"**"=.05,"*"=.1),
              output = 'flextable')


# Forest plot
out_conf <- tidy(post_lasso_model, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  filter(!is.na(conf.low)) %>%  # Filtrer les NA des intervalles de confiance
  filter(term != "(Intercept)")  # Enlever l'intercept

lm_model_out <- round_df(out_conf, digits=2)

# Now plot them
ggplot(lm_model_out, aes(x=reorder(term, estimate), y=estimate)) +
         geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=conf.low, ymax=conf.high), 
                       width = 0.2, size = 1,
                       position = "dodge", color="turquoise4") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red", size = 1) +
  geom_point() + 
  coord_flip()+
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 12)
    ) +
    labs(
      title = "Determinants of Early Childcare Access",
      subtitle = "Post-LASSO predictors",
      x = "",
      y = "Coefficient Estimates"
    )
```
  

# Elastic Nets

## Intention

```{r}


elastic_clean <- MLDummified %>% filter(!is.na(Intention)) %>% 
  mutate(target = as.numeric(Intention) - 1) %>%
 select(-c(Assignment, MovedOut, ECSApp, ECSUseYes, Intention, EntryAgeBeforeOne,BabyHealthIndex, MotherHealthIndex ))%>%      
  mutate(across(where(is.logical), as.numeric)) 



# Preparation
## Split the sample
tidymodels_prefer()
set.seed(153)
elastic_split <- initial_split(elastic_clean, prop = 0.8)
elastic_train <- training(elastic_split)
elastic_test <- testing(elastic_split)

# Apply the recipe (simplified)
model_recipe <- recipe(target ~ ., data = elastic_train) %>%
  step_unknown(AttitudesTowardsWorkAndFamily, AttitudesLaborAffectsChildren) %>% 
    step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE) %>%
    step_zv() %>%
    step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) %>% 
     step_impute_knn(
                  Taux.de.couv.global,
                  NumberChildren,
                  PrescriptiveNorm,
                  neighbors = 5) %>% 
  step_YeoJohnson(
                  NumberChildren, 
                  OpportunityCosts,

                  PrescriptiveNorm
                  #BreastFeedLength,
                  #NumberChildren
                  ) # some variables are skewed. We transform them using YeoJohson that can also deal with missing values


# Specify the metrics: R squared
elastic_metrics <- metric_set(rsq)

# Now with elastic nets we have 2 tuning parameters
elastic_spec <-  linear_reg(penalty = tune(),
                            mixture = tune()) %>%
  set_mode("regression") %>%
  set_engine("glmnet")

# Workflow for elastic nets
elastic_wf <- workflow() %>%
  add_model(elastic_spec) %>%
  add_recipe(model_recipe)

# 10 fold cross validation with 5 repeats
set.seed(20)
cv_folds <- vfold_cv(elastic_train, v = 10, 
                     repeats = 5)

# Tune the model
# First specify the tuning grid with the dials package

# Extract the tuning parameter and store it -- conveniently this way the model knows what are the limits for alpha and lambda
glmnet_param <- extract_parameter_set_dials(elastic_spec)
elastic_grid <- grid_latin_hypercube(glmnet_param, # hypercube when more than 1 tuning parameter, otherwise entropy
                                     size = 175, # number of points in the grid: 50 combinantions of alpha and lambda
                                     variogram_range = 0.5, # influencing how well it explores the parameter space
                                     original = TRUE) # works with the log scale of the lambda

# to tune the model, we use parallel processing (do this as much as you can)
doParallel::registerDoParallel()
elastic_tune <- elastic_wf %>%
  tune_grid(cv_folds, grid = elastic_grid, metrics = elastic_metrics)

autoplot(elastic_tune) # x is different values of lambda in the log scale. y is the average R2

elastic_best <- select_best(elastic_tune)
elastic_best # mixture: 22 percents LASSO and 78 percents Ridge

# Optional: check the values
temp <- collect_metrics(elastic_tune)

# Finalize the model
elastic_updated <- finalize_model(elastic_spec,
                                  elastic_best)
workflow_new <- elastic_wf %>%
  update_model(elastic_updated)

new_fit <- workflow_new %>%
  fit(data = elastic_train)

tidy_elastic <- new_fit %>%
  extract_fit_parsnip() %>%
  tidy()



# Evaluating the model: performance
metrics <- new_fit %>%
  predict(elastic_test) %>%
  bind_cols(elastic_test) %>%
  metrics(truth = target, estimate = .pred)

# R2 here is 0.893, which is a bit better than the lasso


## POST elastic nets 

elastic_var_intention <- tidy_elastic %>% 
  filter(estimate != 0) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  pull(term)  # Liste des variables sélectionnées


## Post EN on training and test sets

# Appliquer la recipe sur les données d'entraînement
elastic_train_baked <- prep(model_recipe) %>% # we preprosess the data
  bake(new_data = elastic_train) # it creates the transformed dataset  

# We do the same for the test set 
elastic_test_baked <- prep(model_recipe) %>% # should we apply the transformatios ? 
  bake(new_data = elastic_test)

# Select only the variables that the elastic picked up
elastic_train_post <- elastic_train_baked %>%
  select(all_of(c("target", elastic_var_intention))) # we select the target and the variables that the elastic picked up

elastic_test_post <- elastic_test_baked %>% # for model metrics
  select(all_of(c("target", elastic_var_intention)))

# Fit the model on the training set 
post_elastic_model <- lm(target ~ ., data = elastic_train_post)


# Accuracy on the test set based on the predicted coefficient
post_elastic_preds <- predict(post_elastic_model, newdata = elastic_test_post)

# Calculer les métriques
post_elastic_metrics <- metrics(
  data = data.frame(truth = elastic_test_post$target, estimate = post_elastic_preds),
  truth = truth,
  estimate = estimate
)

print(post_elastic_metrics)

### Test with the whole dataset

  bake(new_data = elastic_clean) # it creates the dataset normalized and transformed
```

```{r}
## DO THE LASSO 


elastic_clean <- MLDummified_Access %>%
  filter(!is.na(ECSUseYes)) %>%
  mutate(target = as.numeric(ECSUseYes), 
         Applied = ifelse(ECSApp == 1, "Yes", "No" )) %>%
 select(-c( ECSApp, ECSUseYes, EntryAgeBeforeOne))%>%      
  mutate(across(where(is.logical), as.numeric)) 



# Clean the names
coef_names_access <- c(
  "IntentionYes" = "Intention: Household wants to use early childcare after birth",
  "NumberChildren" = "Number of children in the household",
  "Taux.de.couv.global" = "Early childcare coverage in the area of residence",
  "ActiveYes" = "Mother is active before birth",
  "WorkPlanToYes" = "Mother wanted to work after birth",
  "ECAccessHoursFitYes" = "Early childcare opening hours fit",
  "AccessInformalFullTimeYes" = "Houshold has access to informal full-time childcare",
  #"OpportunityCosts" = "Opportunity costs of staying at home for the mother",
  "MonthlyDaycareFees" = "Monthly daycare fees",
  "NegativeImpactSalaryYes" = "Perceived negative impact of staying at home on salary",
  "NegativeImpactCareerYes" = "Perceived negative impact of staying at home on career",
  "NegativeImpactWellBeingYes" = "Perceived negative impact of staying at home on well-being",
  "PrescriptiveNorm" = "Number of people opposed to mother using childcare",
  "NormsUseMostToAllYes" = "The majority of friends and relatives use early childcare",
  "AttitudesTowardsWorkAndFamilyYes" = "Traditional attitudes towards household roles",
  "AttitudesLaborAffectsChildrenYes" = "Believes work negatively affects children",
  "PerceivedAffordabilityOverestimate" = "Overestimates affordability of early childcare",
  "PerceivedAffordabilityUnderestimate" = "Underestimates affordability of early childcare",
  "TrustEarlyChildcareAgreeYes" = "Household trusts early childcare",
  "ECBenefitChildrenAgreeYes" = "Household believes in early childcare benefits",
  "LevelInformationLow knowledge" = "Household has low knowledge about early childcare",
  "LevelComprehensionGoodExcellentYes" = "Mother's comprehension level of French is good/excellent",
  "PresentOrientedYes" = "The mother is present biased",
  "KnowsECIsSubsidizedYes" = "Household knows that early childcare is subsidized",
  "BelieveAccessingChildcareEasyYes" = "Household believes accessing childcare is easy",
  "HasAccessToAComputerYes" = "Household has access to a computer",
  "CanAccessScoialResourcesYes" = "Household can access social resources",
  "CanAccessInformationYes" = "Household can access information",
  "MotherHealthIndex" = "Mother's health index at endline",
  "BabyHealthIndex" = "Baby's health index at endline",
  "AssignmentT1" = "Received Information only",
  "AssignmentT2" = "Received Information + Support",
  #"EntryAgeBeforeOneBefore One" = "Want to use early childcare before the child is 1 yo", 
  "AppliedYes" = "Applied to early childcare at endline",
 # "PoliticalOrientationRight" = "Right-wing mayor",
  #"PoliticalOrientationOther" = "Other political orientation of the mayor",
 "MovedOutYes" = "Household moved between baseline and endline", 
 "ECSAppTimingBeforeBirthYes" = "Applied before birth",
 "IncomeLess than 1500 euros" = "Household income earns less than 1500 euros",
 "IncomeMore than 2500 euros" = "Household income more than 2500 euros", 
       "ApplicationCalledYes" = "Household contacted providers by phone", 
      "ApplicationWentOnSiteYesYes" = "Household visited providers in person",
      "ApplicationNetworkedYes" = "Household reached out to an elected official"
)

# Preparation
## Split the sample
tidymodels_prefer()
set.seed(10)
elastic_split <- initial_split(elastic_clean, prop = 0.8)
elastic_train <- training(elastic_split)
elastic_test <- testing(elastic_split)

# Apply the recipe (simplified)
model_recipe <- recipe(target ~ ., data = elastic_train) %>%
    step_unknown(#EntryAgeBeforeOne, 
                   AttitudesTowardsWorkAndFamily, 
                   AttitudesLaborAffectsChildren 
) %>%   step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE) %>%
    step_zv() %>%
    step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) %>% 
   step_impute_knn(all_numeric_predictors(), neighbors = 5) %>%
  step_YeoJohnson(
                  MotherHealthIndex,
                  BabyHealthIndex,
                  NumberChildren, 
                  #OpportunityCosts,
                  MonthlyDaycareFees,

                  PrescriptiveNorm
                  ) 


# Specify the metrics: R squared
elastic_metrics <- metric_set(rsq)

# Now with elastic nets we have 2 tuning parameters
elastic_spec <-  linear_reg(penalty = tune(),
                            mixture = tune()) %>%
  set_mode("regression") %>%
  set_engine("glmnet")

# Workflow for elastic nets
elastic_wf <- workflow() %>%
  add_model(elastic_spec) %>%
  add_recipe(model_recipe)

# 10 fold cross validation with 5 repeats
set.seed(20)
cv_folds <- vfold_cv(elastic_train, v = 10, 
                     repeats = 5)

# Tune the model
# First specify the tuning grid with the dials package

# Extract the tuning parameter and store it -- conveniently this way the model knows what are the limits for alpha and lambda
glmnet_param <- extract_parameter_set_dials(elastic_spec)
elastic_grid <- grid_latin_hypercube(glmnet_param, # hypercube when more than 1 tuning parameter, otherwise entropy
                                     size = 175, # number of points in the grid: 50 combinantions of alpha and lambda
                                     variogram_range = 0.75, # influencing how well it explores the parameter space
                                     original = TRUE) # works with the log scale of the lambda

# to tune the model, we use parallel processing (do this as much as you can)
doParallel::registerDoParallel()
elastic_tune <- elastic_wf %>%
  tune_grid(cv_folds, grid = elastic_grid, metrics = elastic_metrics)

autoplot(elastic_tune) # x is different values of lambda in the log scale. y is the average R2

elastic_best <- select_best(elastic_tune)
elastic_best # mixture: 22 percents LASSO and 78 percents Ridge

# Optional: check the values
temp <- collect_metrics(elastic_tune)

# Finalize the model
elastic_updated <- finalize_model(elastic_spec,
                                  elastic_best)
workflow_new <- elastic_wf %>%
  update_model(elastic_updated)

new_fit <- workflow_new %>%
  fit(data = elastic_train)

tidy_elastic <- new_fit %>%
  extract_fit_parsnip() %>%
  tidy()



# Evaluating the model: performance
metrics <- new_fit %>%
  predict(elastic_test) %>%
  bind_cols(elastic_test) %>%
  metrics(truth = target, estimate = .pred)

# R2 here is 0.893, which is a bit better than the lasso


## POST elastic nets 

elastic_var_access <- tidy_elastic %>% 
  filter(estimate != 0) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  pull(term)  # Liste des variables sélectionnées



## Post EN on training and test sets

# Appliquer la recipe sur les données d'entraînement
elastic_train_baked <- prep(model_recipe) %>% # we preprosess the data
  bake(new_data = elastic_train) # it creates the transformed dataset  

# We do the same for the test set 
elastic_test_baked <- prep(model_recipe) %>% # should we apply the transformatios ? 
  bake(new_data = elastic_test)

# Select only the variables that the elastic picked up
elastic_train_post <- elastic_train_baked %>%
  select(all_of(c("target", elastic_var_access))) # we select the target and the variables that the elastic picked up

elastic_test_post <- elastic_test_baked %>% # for model metrics
  select(all_of(c("target", elastic_var_access)))

# Fit the model on the training set 
post_elastic_model <- lm(target ~ ., data = elastic_train_post)


# Accuracy on the test set based on the predicted coefficient
post_elastic_preds <- predict(post_elastic_model, newdata = elastic_test_post)

# Calculer les métriques
post_elastic_metrics <- metrics(
  data = data.frame(truth = elastic_test_post$target, estimate = post_elastic_preds),
  truth = truth,
  estimate = estimate
)
print(post_elastic_metrics)

### Test with the whole dataset
# Appliquer la recipe sur les données d'entraînement
elastic_train_baked <- prep(model_recipe) %>% # we preprosess the data
  bake(new_data = elastic_clean) # it creates the dataset normalized and transformed


# Select only the variables that the elastic picked up
elastic_train_post <- elastic_train_baked %>%
  select(all_of(c("target", elastic_var_access))) # we select the target and the variables that the elastic picked up

# Fit the model on the training set 
post_elastic_model <- lm(target ~ ., data = elastic_train_post)

# Extraire les coefficients et autres informations du modèle
coefficients_table <- tidy(post_elastic_model) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(estimate))) %>% # Trier par ordre décroissant de la valeur absolue des coefficients
  mutate(estimate = round(estimate, 3),  # Arrondir pour améliorer la lisibilité
         std.error = round(std.error, 3))
# Sélectionner les colonnes importantes

library(modelsummary)


# 1. Extraire et trier les coefficients avec broom::tidy
tidied <- tidy(post_elastic_model) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(estimate))) # Trier par ordre décroissant de la valeur absolue des coefficients

# 2. Utiliser coef_map pour réorganiser les coefficients dans modelsummary
modelsummary(list("Access" =post_elastic_model),
             statistic = "{std.error} ({p.value})",
             estimate="{estimate}{stars}  [{conf.low}, {conf.high}]",
             coef_map = setNames(tidied$term, tidied$term), # Réorganiser les coefficients dans l'ordre trié
             #gof_map = c("nobs", "r.squared", "adj.r.squared", "AIC", "BIC"), # Inclure les statistiques globales
             stars = c("***"=.01,"**"=.05,"*"=.1),
              output = 'flextable') %>% autofit()

# Forest plot
out_conf <- tidy(post_elastic_model, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  filter(!is.na(conf.low)) %>%  # Filtrer les NA des intervalles de confiance
  filter(term != "(Intercept)")  # Enlever l'intercept

elastic_model_out <- round_df(out_conf, digits=2)

# Now plot them
ggplot(elastic_model_out, aes(x=reorder(term, estimate), y=estimate)) +
         geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=conf.low, ymax=conf.high), 
                       width = 0.2, size = 1,
                       position = "dodge", color="turquoise4") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red", size = 1) +
  geom_point() + 
  coord_flip()+
     theme_minimal() +
     theme(
       axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
       plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
       axis.title = element_text(size = 12)
     ) +
     labs(
       title = "Determinants of Early Childcare Access",
       subtitle = "Elastic-Nets predictors",
       x = "",
       y = "Coefficient Estimates"
     )
```

```{r}
elastic_var_access <- clean_variable_names(elastic_var_access)


# Clean the names
coef_names_access <- c(
  "IntentionYes" = "Intention: Household wants to use early childcare after birth",
  "NumberChildren" = "Number of children in the household",
  "Taux.de.couv.global" = "Early childcare coverage in the area of residence",
  "ActiveYes" = "Mother is active before birth",
  "WorkPlanToYes" = "Mother wanted to work after birth",
  "ECAccessHoursFitYes" = "Early childcare opening hours fit",
  "AccessInformalFullTimeYes" = "Houshold has access to informal full-time childcare",
  "OpportunityCosts" = "Opportunity costs of staying at home for the mother",
  "NegativeImpactSalaryYes" = "Perceived negative impact of staying at home on salary",
  "NegativeImpactCareerYes" = "Perceived negative impact of staying at home on career",
  "NegativeImpactWellBeingYes" = "Perceived negative impact of staying at home on well-being",
  "PrescriptiveNorm" = "Number of people opposed to mother using childcare",
  "NormsUseMostToAllYes" = "The majority of friends and relatives use early childcare",
  "AttitudesTowardsWorkAndFamilyYes" = "Traditional attitudes towards household roles",
  "AttitudesLaborAffectsChildrenYes" = "Believes work negatively affects children",
  "PerceivedAffordabilityOverestimate" = "Overestimates affordability of early childcare",
  "PerceivedAffordabilityUnderestimate" = "Underestimates affordability of early childcare",
  "TrustEarlyChildcareAgreeYes" = "Household trusts early childcare",
  "ECBenefitChildrenAgreeYes" = "Household believes in early childcare benefits",
  "LevelInformationLow knowledge" = "Household has low knowledge about early childcare",
  "LevelComprehensionGoodExcellentYes" = "Mother's comprehension level of French is good/excellent",
  "PresentOrientedYes" = "The mother is present biased",
  "KnowsECIsSubsidizedYes" = "Household knows that early childcare is subsidized",
  "BelieveAccessingChildcareEasyYes" = "Household believes accessing childcare is easy",
  "HasAccessToAComputerYes" = "Household has access to a computer",
  "CanAccessScoialResourcesYes" = "Household can access social resources",
  "CanAccessInformationYes" = "Household can access information",
  "MotherHealthIndex" = "Mother's health index at endline",
  "BabyHealthIndex" = "Baby's health index at endline",
  "AssignmentT1" = "Received Information only",
  "AssignmentT2" = "Received Information + Support",
  "EntryAgeBeforeOneBefore One" = "Want to use early childcare before the child is 1 yo", 
  "AppliedYes" = "Applied to early childcare at endline",
  "MovedOutYes" = "Household moved between baseline and endline"

)


oaxaca_data_access <- Oaxaca %>%
  filter(!is.na(ECSUseYes)) %>%
  mutate(
    target = as.numeric(ECSUseYes),
    Educ_bin = as.numeric(Educ == "Sup"),
    Applied = factor(ifelse(ECSApp == 1, "Yes", "No" )) )%>%   # Convert to binary: 1 for "Sup", 0 for "Bac"=) %>%
  select(target, Educ_bin, all_of(elastic_var_access))    

# Create formula using clean_vars with proper oaxaca syntax
formula_vars <- paste(elastic_var_access, collapse = " + ")
formula_str <- paste("target ~ ", formula_vars, " | Educ_bin")
oax_formula <- as.formula(formula_str)

set.seed(124)
 # Level of comprehension creates pb
# Run Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition
oax_elastic_access <- oaxaca(formula = oax_formula,
                     data = oaxaca_data_access,
                     R = 100)  # Number of bootstrap repetitions

# Plot the share of the gap explained by the variables
gapExplained <- plot_oaxaca_gap(oax_elastic_access, 
                                outcome = "Access",
                                model = "Elastic-Nets predictors")
gapExplained

```
